commits.headline: fix(voice): report a pending output route, parse the toggle payload, trim tests
commits.body:
An unresolved output leg (routeState preferred_candidate) no longer reads as
untrusted_route on a trusted input: it is route_pending, an idle lamp and an
info log line, until the first playback resolves the route. An untrusted input
stays definitive and a degraded system fallback stays untrusted.
toggle_barge_any_route now takes a boolean or true/false/on/off, flips on an
absent payload and ignores anything else with a [barge] warning. The existing
trusted-AEC engaged/released console line is cl

commits.headline: fix(voice): free a rejected pin before the .env retry and cancel stale unloads
commits.body:
A pinned model can load and then fail the production-dialect probe; the
boot fallback switched to the .env model while that checkpoint stayed
resident. fallBackToEnv now unloads what the abandoned pin loaded (tools
and chat halves, never the .env model or TTS) before the retry, which
also replaces the pair-only cleanup in proveChatHalf.

commits.headline: fix(visual): space the sleep-flash blink shots one phase apart and check them
commits.body:
Each blink phase lasts 250 ms, so the 125 ms gap could land both shots in
the same phase. Shots now sit 250 ms apart. VHS still jitters around its
8 fps frame grid, so the script requires the 150x38 pair to differ
(capturing again, three attempts in all) and the reduced-motion pair to
match.

commits.headline: fix(voice): drop LiveKit from the EOT bench sidecar and harden Smart Turn errors
commits.body:
The LiveKit model licence only allows use with LiveKit Agents, so the sidecar
now scores Smart Turn v3 only: no /score/livekit, no runner loading, no
livekit dependency (re-locked), and /health is {ok, smart_turn}.

commits.headline: fix(voice): count a fired wake that follows a rejected line in the same burst
commits.body:
A burst that opened with a below_threshold or verifier_rejected WAKE line
reported as one rejection even when a fired WAKE line or an accepted wake
followed it in the same window, so the fire never reached fires, the
playback count or the threshold input. Prefer a fired WAKE line, and treat
any non-manual WAKE_ACCEPTED as a fire.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): key the agent prompt off its own action notice
commits.body:
Hub.Notice is shared with unrelated UI: a workspace preferences save
failure writes it too. While an agent compose was open, such a notice
replaced the draft, made Enter refuse a valid send, and was wiped by the
next keystroke.

commits.body:

an intra-function dead branch, so everything it called still looked live: the

that is no longer drawn, the input-dock click, the sidecar clicks and the

commits.body: A v* tag still opens the GitHub release. npm publish and the binary build wait until the PUBLISH_NPM repository variable is true.

commits.headline: feat(cockpit): add a palette row that toggles barge-in on any device
commits.body:
The voice agent runs barge-in only on the trusted echo-cancelling route
(PowerConf in and out). The new "barge any device" row sends
toggle_barge_any_route so the operator can opt in on any other route
and back out again. It sends no enabled flag, so the agent flips its
current setting.

commits.headline: fix(voice): keep the BARGE_ROUTE line to the agreed field order
commits.body:
Drop the extra why= token from the BARGE_ROUTE transcript/stderr line and key
the change-only reporter on enabled, reason, any_route and both labels. The
route verdict stays on the barge lamp detail and in runtime.status bargeRoute.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): hold Enter while a hub notice hides the agent draft
commits.body:
After a failed reply or redirect the dock shows the failure notice in
place of the draft and advertises "type to edit · esc cancel", but Enter
still resent the hidden draft with the attention version captured when
the compose began. After a "question changed" conflict that repeats a
request already known to be stale. Enter now waits until an edit clears
the notice, so it only ever sends the draft the operator can see.

commits.headline: fix(voice): re-prove models voice unloaded and both halves of a pinned pair
commits.body:
A picker switch back to an MLX model voice had unloaded trusted
mlxBypassReady and skipped the probe, so a failed reload left an
acknowledged route that could not answer. Voice now remembers the models
it unloaded (any served spelling) and re-proves one before switching to
it, from the picker or a spoken switch; a failed re-proof changes nothing
and no longer reads as local-eligible.

commits.headline: feat(workspace): draw the s sleep/listen flash on the v2 frame
commits.body:
The flash from #112 and #114 lived only in the legacy chip row and
statusline, which the live Workspace v2 frame never drew. The state was
live (the next s toggles from it, and the tick raises the frame rate for
it), but nothing showed it.

commits.headline: fix(voice): show whether barge-in is running, with an any-device override
commits.body:
The barge lamp read armed on every SPEAKING entry even when the route was not
trusted and barge-in never ran. One syncBargeAvailability now drives the lamp
(degraded on an untrusted route, off in wake-word-only), a BARGE_ROUTE
transcript line plus a [barge] route stderr line on change, and a bargeRoute
block in runtime.status. VOICE_BARGE_ANY_ROUTE and the toggle_barge_any_route
bridge command let the operator enable barge-in on any route. The cockpit logs
panel would have shown the new stderr l

commits.headline: feat(voice): resolve barge-in availability and the any-route override
commits.body:
Add a pure availability resolver for barge-in (wake-word-only, trusted AEC
route, any-route override, untrusted route), its transcript line formatter, a
change-only reporter, and the barge lamp reading, in barge/route-availability.js.
shouldEvaluateBargeIn gains anyRoute, which skips the trusted-AEC requirement;
every existing caller is unchanged. Export lineSafe from the gate ledger so the
new line shares its sanitiser.

commits.headline: fix(release): publish a public manifest from the private repo root
commits.body: npm refuses a private workspace package. The release job now writes dist/package.json without private or workspaces, and the repo root stays private.

commits.headline: feat(voice): add the offline end-of-turn scoring sidecar
commits.body:
Adds services/eot-bench, a bench-only FastAPI sidecar on 127.0.0.1:8783 that
scores transcripts with the LiveKit turn detector and 16 kHz audio with Smart
Turn v3. It is never on the voice runtime path; scripts/eot-bench.js (next
task) is its only caller.

commits.headline: feat(voice): add the wake-word activity report with tuning suggestions
commits.body:
Parse WAKE / WAKE_ACCEPTED transcript lines, USER lines and the
voice-wake-scores.jsonl records into one activation per burst, then
report per-model fires, rejections, near misses and playback fires,
with suggested OPENWAKEWORD_PATIENCE_FRAMES and per-model thresholds.
Keyboard wakes are counted but excluded from the suggestions, and
score records without an outcome never count as fires.

commits.headline: fix(cockpit): ignore acks from a superseded default pin too
commits.body:
A late model.set_default ack for a pin a newer ctrl+d replaced would
overwrite StatusHint and announce the older model as the default while
the catalog and the star show the newer one. The superseded-pin guard
now covers acknowledgements as well as errors.

fix(workspace): show hub action errors in the agent dock while composing
commits.body:
The Agents-tab dock row showed Hub.Notice only when no compose was active.
Once a reply, redirect or stop failed and kept its draft, the row went back
to "To X › draft▌" and the reason ("question changed · not retried") was
drawn nowhere. The removed legacy footer was the only place that showed it.
The recovery confirmation had the same gap for "· retry confirmation
retained".

commits.body:
A model.set_default command.error for a ctrl+d that a newer pin replaced
no longer reaches StatusHint, LastError or the optimistic star. The
newest dispatched pin id is kept apart from PendingModelDefault because
any model.catalog clears the pending pin, and a genuine error for the
latest pin can arrive after one.

The cloud turn lit the lamp for the whole generateVoiceTurn() attempt, so a
client tool running between provider rounds still read as a busy brain.
Begin on each model_request_start and release on model_request_end, ahead of
onStatus's abort/turn guard so a late end still releases, and release any

commits.body:

commits.headline: fix(voice): read a mic suppressed by the user talking as open
commits.body:
MIC_READY_SUPPRESSED mapped every reason to an amber mic lamp. When the
reason is user_speaking the mic is open and hearing the user, and nothing
retries the suppression, so the lamp stayed amber through the user's turn and
the reply (a median of 38 s, about one ready cycle in five last month). Read
it as pass; the other reasons, where the mic is not open for a new turn yet,
stay hold.

commits.body:
Wire the gate ledger into the voice agent (spec WS2a): one gate.state bridge
event and one GATE transcript line per gate decision, one GATES summary per
turn, and a gates snapshot in runtime.status so the cockpit recovers its lamps
on reconnect. VOICE_GATE_LEDGER and VOICE_GATE_LEDGER_LOG (both default true)
turn the ledger and its transcript lines off.

full gate-ledger readings (spec WS2a), so the agent's hook sites stay one-line
calls and every mapping is unit-tested against payloads copied from the real

commits.headline: fix(voice): preserve queries when joining MLX endpoints (#2129)
commits.body:
MLX proxy bases with query strings appended the API suffix inside the
query, sending requests to the wrong path and losing a query value's
trailing slash. A shared URL helper now appends the fixed suffix to
pathname, preserving the prefix and original query; model-list cache
keys retain distinct queries.

commits.headline: fix(cli): skip covered controls in snapshot refs and role clicks
commits.body: Role and ref clicks now use the same visibility check as text clicks, including one parent frame when the control sits in a nested iframe. Snapshot refs use that check too, so a hidden frame or an overlay is not a click target.

commits.headline: fix(cli): keep snapshot roots and names inside the right tree
commits.body: An empty href is still a link, a hidden main is not the snapshot root, and a custom-element main or dialog walks its own shadow root. Label lookup can see a sibling outside main, but it stops at the shadow root.

commits.headline: fix(brand): crop the toolbar glove to the solid bone
commits.body: The bright cyan plume passed the luminance row test, so the crop still included the wrist trail. Count low-chroma bone only, and clear the trail that hangs beside the longer fingers.

commits.headline: fix(voice): ignore non-plain objects as gate readings
commits.body:
isPlainObject accepted any non-array object, so a Date, Map or class
instance reaching set() was read as an empty full reading that cleared the
gate. Accept only object literals and null-prototype objects, as the
contract says. Found by Codex on #2128.

commits.headline: fix(cli): bound steps and keep snapshot and evaluate data
commits.body: Evaluate source is no longer rewritten by placeholder substitution, snapshot url and title stay in the step result, and the command deadline stops the sequence.

commits.headline: fix(cli): keep validation alerts in the scoped snapshot

commits.headline: fix(finance): the dotenv guard also catches dotenv's KEY: value form
commits.body:
wrangler parses .env and .env.local with the dotenv package, which accepts
`KEY: value` as well as `KEY=value`. util.parseEnv only reads the latter, so
`CLOUDFLARE_ENV: staging` would have passed the I1 guard while wrangler still
applied it. A line-anchored check for the key with dotenv's two separators

commits.headline: fix(finance): do not refresh Plaid freshness when no bank refreshed
commits.body:
A Wise-only success republished the unchanged bank rows with a new
synced_at. Freshness is the oldest anchor, so the dashboard read "Synced 5m
ago" over stale bank data. The two Plaid snapshots are now written only when
a bank merged or an upload unlinked a bank whose rows were dropped; the
ledger is still rebuilt from the served rows.

commits.headline: fix(finance): advance a Plaid cursor only from the delta the ledger merged
commits.body:
The step returned next_cursor and accounts while the ledger merged whatever
the R2 object held, so a step attempt that timed out and wrote late could
leave the ledger with one attempt's rows and the item with another's cursor.
Each attempt now writes its delta (with the cursor and the stripped accounts
inside it) under its own key, buildRunLedger reports the deltas it merged,
and publish advances cursors from that list only.

commits.headline: fix(finance): take the finance lock for accounting edits
commits.body:
The /accounting/* write routes (transaction and account edits, manual
entries, rules, vendor meta, reconciliation, AI propose, accept and
dismiss) rewrite overrides, manual entries and AI proposals and rebuild
the ledger without the finance lock. An edit during a scheduled refresh
could interleave two rebuilds, or publish new state beside a ledger
built from the old one.

commits.headline: fix(finance): reclaim a stale lock without deleting a live one
commits.body:
Reclaiming read the holder, compared it, then unlinked the path. Between
the read and the unlink another process could reclaim the same stale lock
and create its own, and the unlink then removed that live lock, leaving
two writers. Release had the same read-then-unlink shape.

commits.headline: fix(finance): lock every Plaid item mutation; spot worktrees; quiet publish
commits.body:
Link, rename and disconnect in local dev rewrite plaid-items.json too, so a
scheduled refresh that read the store first could write it back stale and
restore a disconnected bank. They now take the finance lock (link before the
Plaid exchange, so a busy lock never drops a new token) and answer 409 while a
refresh holds it.

commits.headline: docs: design hosted finance sync (Phase 5a)
commits.body:
Phase 5 splits into 5a (finance syncing on the host) and 5b (finance writes).
5a moves Plaid and Wise sync and the ledger rebuild to a Cloudflare Workflow on
a 6h cron plus an owner-only Refresh, with credentials encrypted on the Mac and
written via wrangler, and a shadow mode so the first hosted ledger is compared
with a local rebuild before it serves anything.

commits.headline: docs: disclose published customer PII and set WPF_REMOTE_API in step 6
commits.body:
publish:snapshots uploads every top-level data/live file, including the
EDD files that carry customer names and emails. SYNC.md said those never
leave the machine. It and DEPLOY.md now say they go to the private,
Access-gated R2 bucket (principals only) and that staging gets fixtures.

commits.headline: fix(publish): keep accounting-state slugs out of the live-directory pass
commits.body:
A state file found in data/live (accounting-overrides, plaid-status, ...)
still published under accounting-state, so includeState:false (--no-state)
could return a state bundle and a stale live copy could publish when the
secure source was absent. The live pass now checks PUBLISHED_LIVE_SLUGS
only; state publishes solely from data/secure.

commits.headline: fix(worker): cap publish bodies at 10 MB and decode them as they stream
commits.body:
A 50 MB body could not fit a 128 MB Worker isolate once it was decoded,
parsed and re-serialised per envelope, and readTextWithin held every raw
chunk plus a combined copy before decoding.

commits.headline: fix(publish): publish only an explicit allowlist of data/live slugs
commits.body:
A valid filename was treated as permission to publish, so operational
exports that share data/live (presale and renewal outreach queues, CRM
sync audits, the payout queue, customer-health-by-email) would upload
customer PII in the edd bundle. PUBLISHED_LIVE_SLUGS now lists the files
the hosted copy reads: the file-backed UI endpoints, the accounting view
inputs and the freshness anchors. A contract test fails when a UI
endpoint or freshness anchor is missing from it.

commits.body:

owners with the GitHub tools still loaded. While the session holds a

section (localGithubSessionSection). With no GitHub grant the prompt is
byte-identical; a grant already rebuilds and re-warms the prefix.

recall that turn is as unbacked as a claimed tool result, and none of the
existing claim detectors cover it.

commits.headline: Default the speaker-embed sidecar to CAM++ common_advanced
commits.body:
A 13-model bake-off on LibriSpeech dev-clean (20 owners with 3-clip
centroids, 19 impostors each, 20 disjoint cohort speakers) put the old
English VoxCeleb CAM++ at 13.5% EER on clean 6s turns and 19% / 27% under
5 dB / 0 dB three-talker babble. 3D-Speaker's common_advanced CAM++ scored
0% clean and 1.0% / 8.5% under babble, ahead of TitaNet small/large and
ERes2NetV2 under noise, at the same size (~28MB) and speed (~21ms per
second of audio on one CPU thread).

Codex review: requiring a determiner after run/running dropped real
undertakings with a bare-noun object ("I'm running tests now", "I'll run
diagnostics now", "Let me run npm test now"). run/running now count unless

character cap could cut the words off and quote the cards instead. The
directive now quotes only what follows BACKGROUND_MEMORY_REQUEST_LABEL,

commits.headline: fix(voice): "running" with no object is a state, not an undertaking
commits.body:
Live 2026-10-09 on the Qwen3.8 distill, "I'm running now on that Qwen 3.8
distill" and "that's what I'm running now per my notes" matched the
first-person undertaking pattern (I'm + running + now), and the claim
guard's retry replaced a correct greeting. run/running now count as an
undertaking stem only with an object word straight after ("I'm running
the script now", "I'll run it now"). The other stems are unchanged.

commits.headline: fix(voice): the claim-guard directive quotes the user turn it corrects
commits.body:
Every corrective directive opened "Answer my original request directly".
With the session warm-up exchange pinned at the head of history, that is
ambiguous, and on 2026-10-09 the Qwen3.8 distill answered the warm-up
line ("reply with one short word") instead of Jack.

commits.headline: fix(gauntlet): bound the runtime plane's warm-up request
commits.body:
Codex review: the plane awaits the warm-up, which had no first-byte
deadline and no signal, so a server that accepted the request and never
sent a byte would hang a whole nightly or A/B run. It now carries the
per-round bound (MODEL_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, 120 s), combined with any
caller signal. A failed warm-up is still not cached.

commits.headline: feat(gauntlet): the runtime plane pins production's warm-up exchange
commits.body:
Every live local turn carries the session warm-up at the head of history:
"Session check — reply with one short word." and the model's own
temperature-0 reply. The runtime plane never sent it, so it measured a
history production never sends. On 2026-10-09 a live claim retry ("answer
my original request") answered the warm-up line instead of Jack; the
plane could not reproduce that.

it checks out. A manual run from the Actions tab defaults to main, so it
would test the PR but leave its required checks on main. Read the PR's
head and fail fast, naming the branch to run from, when the run is not on

would, so the cloud prompt keeps MEMORY_RECALL_GUIDANCE; "baseline": false
keeps the no-grounding path. The dry run reports which cases lack the
guidance.

refusal notice and the user turn that drew it, and the prefetch
re-ingested that turn's screenshot as an image on every turn.

commits.headline: fix(voice): clarify soft barge handling

commits.body:

repeat delay (~0.5s on macOS), outside the 250ms cadence window, so holding
s toggled sleep then wake. Hold the first key after an accepted press to a
750ms initial window, then slide the 250ms window once a repeat stream is
recognised.

Code session (about 30 tasks, each fanned out to every d

(buildNotes) and the response assembly (renderRecallResponse) out of

response it actually assembles. No behavior change: the existing recall

commits.headline: fix(client): accept a Unicode zero as the start of a 0x prefix
commits.body:
Python's int() reads every Unicode decimal digit as its ASCII value
before parsing, so uuid.UUID("٠x" + 30 hex digits) is valid: "٠x" is a
radix prefix. The regex only recognized an ASCII "0x" and refused that
spelling. Capture the prefix digit and accept it when it is a zero.
Unicode encodes each decimal digit set as a contiguous 0-9 run, so a
digit's value is its distance from the start of its run, mod 10.

commits.body:
Text output never said which results scope_fallback admitted from
outside the requested tags, and items output dropped the notes
entirely. Mark each such result with " [outside tag scope]" in text and

commits.headline: fix(recall): keep t_valid, t_invalid and archived in json and ID-fetch output
commits.body:
Result normalization copied a fixed field list and dropped the node
state that explains why a current_only: false or state_mode: "history"
recall returned a memory. Map t_valid, t_invalid and archived on the
ranked, ID-fetch and enumeration paths, and emit them in the unbudgeted
outputs (format: "json" and ID fetch). Budgeted text/items/detailed
stay compact.

commits.headline: fix(client): refuse memory ids the API would reject before they reach a URL path
commits.body:
fetchMemoryById, updateMemory and deleteMemory put the caller's id
straight into the request path. encodeURIComponent stops "/", "?" and
"#" but not "." or a whole segment that names another route, so
"by-tag" reached GET and DELETE /memory/by-tag and ".." normalized to
"/". None of these returned or deleted data, but the next route added
under /memory/ would be reachable by id.

commits.headline: fix(recall): reject params a recall mode cannot honor and correct the schema
commits.body:
Enumeration mode (`exhaustive: true`) now rejects context, language,
active_path, context_tags, context_types, priority_ids and
per_query_limit. GET /memory/by-tag reads only tags, limit and offset,
so these were silently ignored and an audit looked prioritized when it
was not.

commits.headline: fix(recall): return recall errors as isError tool results
commits.body:
The recall_memory case returned buildRecallMemoryResponse's promise from
inside the handler's try without awaiting it, so a rejection skipped the
catch and reached clients as a JSON-RPC -32603 error. Await it so recall
failures come back as `Error: <msg>` with isError: true, like the other
five tools.

commits.body:
A failed `gh pr view` also returns null, so a transient GitHub error on an
oversized branch could be recorded as a terminal split even though a PR
existed. The split now requires the run-branch target and a positive empty
`gh pr list --head <branch> --state all`; anything else keeps the
pr_resolution failure.

commits.headline: fix(mobile): alert again when a retried task blocks again
commits.body:
Retry keeps the task id, so a second blocked outcome shared the first
one's semantic dedupe key and was dropped as a persisted duplicate; with
the finalizer child deferring to its parent, a retried split sent nothing.
A blocked alert now carries its attempt id (the row version on a legacy
row) and the dedupe key includes it, so each attempt alerts once and a
replay of the same block stays one alert.

commits.headline: fix(mobile): alert once when a hub task ends blocked
commits.body:
A task that stopped as blocked (a split, a blocked PR) had no mobile
transition, and with a finalizer child's failure deferred to its parent,
nothing reached the phone. The move into blocked now sends one push_feed
alert as task_failed with payload.status blocked, which the app renders in
Needs You: the agent's name as title, the task as subtitle, and the
result summary (or error) as body.

commits.headline: fix(api): keep the plan and question options whole in excerpt mode
commits.body:
?excerpt=true clamped attentionPlan and attentionQuestions to 1 KiB per
string, the same cap as lifecycle and context. The AutoJack Inbox card
renders attentionPlan.markdown with Approve/Revise, so a plan approved from
a REST-only load (cold start, push open) would be approved after seeing
only its first 1 KiB, with no marker on the card.

commits.headline: fix(agents): make the size-gate split readable as a push body
commits.body:
The split message now leads with a sentence that stands alone in a
220-character push: "Too large for one PR: <N> changed lines on
<branch>. Split proposed, no PR opened." It then says where the work and
the split plan live, and asks Jack to reply or re-dispatch with the slices
he wants instead of approving a split nothing can act on. The finalizer
prompt asks the babysit child for the same sentence as its blocker reason,
because that reason is the body of the child's own failure push.

commits.headline: fix(workflows): report a failed issue comment as failed in Slack
commits.body:
With the PAT fallback gone, a failed App mint makes the issue comment
POST return 401. The optional http step assigns GitHub's error body,
which has no `ok` field, so the Slack step's `ok !== false` check
reported "Comment posted". Derive `posted` from the created comment's
html_url instead. This also stops claiming a post when no comment was
attempted.

commits.headline: fix(github): never reply to agents posting as Jack; App-only workflow writes
commits.body:
The AutoApp daily-iteration Claude routine comments on AutoApp#426
through the Claude GitHub App with Jack's user token. The comment arrives
with user jack-arturo (type User), passes the bot guard, and fires a
reply_to_author orchestrator run every weekday at 11:04Z. GitHub marks
those comments with performed_via_github_app; comments Jack types leave
it null (1734 of 1734 on autohub). The classifier now ignores
app-mediated comments for reply_to_author. Explicit @mentions still
dispatch.

commits.headline: fix(agents): headline a stopped delivery with its delivery report
commits.body:
The worker's terminal write for a blocked or ready-for-merge delivery kept
the implementer's earlier handoff summary as result_summary, so a size-gate
split still read "verified implementation handoff". Both kernel and legacy
completion writes now carry the delivery report's summary for stopped
deliveries, as the in-process task-queue path already does. The finalizer
prompt also names --blocker-reason, which the CLI needs before it attaches
the size blocker type.

commits.headline: fix(agents): end an oversized change as a split, not a permission prompt
commits.body:
When babysit stops at its preflight size gate before any PR exists, the
finalizer now records a verified `split_required` blocked receipt instead
of failing pr_resolution. It verifies the stop from structured facts only:
the child's attempt-scoped blocked present_result, no PR, and a measured
`git diff --shortstat origin/<base>...HEAD` over 900 lines. The receipt
carries the branch, head, changed lines and the bounded split plan, and a
recovered parent reuses it for the same head.

Fixes #1341: a detector result marked `clipped-response-audio` was being

commits.headline: Retry Agent UI fixture starts that lose the free-port race
commits.body:
freePort() bound port 0, closed the probe, and returned the number, so
nothing held the port until the fixture bound it. Three back-to-back
probes could also return the same port twice. Hosted Pre-merge CI hit
this as `listen EADDRINUSE 127.0.0.1:38155` (run 37468101978).

commits.headline: fix(reflection): preserve indented evidence markers (#2010)
commits.body:
Nested quote markers such as `> > text` left a literal `>` in evidence
passages, while four-space-indented code lost literal quote/bullet
markers. Strip nested quote markers across horizontal spaces/tabs, and
limit quote/list marker removal to lines with at most three initial
spaces. The existing pipeline handles these rules before whitespace
normalization and sentence selection.

commits.headline: fix(slack): focus replies on the triggering message (#1996)
commits.body:
When AutoJack is mentioned in a channel, older questions can compete
with the triggering message. This change marks the incoming message as
the reply target and frames earlier channel/thread messages and search
context as background, while retaining directly relevant thread and
topic references.

commits.headline: fix(agents): target only open PRs that the base does not already contain
commits.body:
A mention on a merged PR in a merge-commit repository (AutoApp) passed the
ancestry guard, since the merged head is in main and in every run cut from
it. The finalizer then told its child to push onto the dead branch. A
candidate PR must now be OPEN, and its head must not already be in
origin/<base>; otherwise resolution falls through to the next source.

commits.headline: fix(api): clamp object results on full-row task_status frames in excerpt mode
commits.body:
The reconciler (and worker/queue emitters) build task_status frames from raw
runtime tasks whose parsed `result` is an object, and they skip
serializeAgentRunForClient, which is what stringifies it. The excerpt only
cuts strings, so an object result passed through untouched and reported
resultTruncated false with a zero full length.

commits.headline: fix(home-assistant): gate Lennard indicator on pulse state
fix(api): bound full-row task_status frames in the task-events excerpt mode
commits.body:
The PR reconciler emits task_status as {...refreshedTask, lifecycle}, a whole
runtime task with raw result, context and tool history. The excerpt mode only
capped lifecycle on task_status, so such a frame stayed multi-megabyte for a
client that asked for excerpt=true.

commits.headline: fix(agents): give each babysit finalizer run its own cancellation signal
commits.body:
task-control cancels the finalizer child by marking its row, which never
aborts the stage signal, so a cancel that landed while a continuation's
executor was still setting up let that run launch and keep working. Each run
now checks the row before launching and polls it while live, aborting the
run's signal on a cancel; the executor then kills the session.

commits.headline: fix(agents): finalize the pull request the task worked on
commits.body:
The babysit finalizer looked up its PR by the run's own worktree branch.
A task that named an existing PR (agent-fp-0cc4c3c0, AutoApp #427) pushed
its fixes to that PR's branch, then failed with "finished without an open
pull request for agent/kernel-worker/a1414579".

commits.headline: feat(api): bound task-events SSE rows behind an opt-in ?excerpt=true
commits.body:
GET /v1/tasks/events (and the /api/agent-tasks/events alias) serialized full
task rows. One row with a 725K result and 164K prompt made the iOS app's
initial_tasks frame 3.27 MB, re-downloaded on every reconnect, and later
task_updated/task_completed frames carried the same rows.

commits.headline: test(push-gateway): pin delivery when the first APNs answer outlasts the prime wait
commits.body:
A local review argued that fanning out after a quarter of the deadline,
before a slow first answer, gets the rest refused again. It does not: by
then the session holds the server's advertised one-stream limit, and the
client queues the remaining streams until the limit is raised. Share the
cold-session server between both tests and add the slow-first case
(500 ms first answer, 250 ms prime wait): 17 of 17 delivered.

commits.headline: test(mobile): cover a hub task session read from the store
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: refactor(mobile): parse a task's context once in the parent alert policy
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(agents): read the finalizer row after the label so a late cancel is seen
commits.body:
task-control kills the session before it marks the row cancelled, so a
cancel could land while the in-flight label read awaited GitHub and a
continuation would still spawn. Reading the row last leaves no await between
the cancellation check and the next execute().

commits.headline: fix(mobile): collapse an agent task's alerts on the task, not its conversation
commits.body:
Two tasks dispatched from one iOS conversation shared a collapse id, so one
task's question replaced the other's on the lock screen. Agent task pushes now
collapse on task:<id>:<event>; the thread id, which groups and routes them,
is unchanged.

commits.headline: fix(mobile): leave a finalizer's failure to its parent's alert
commits.body:
A babysit finalizer child failed and pushed its own alert, titled with the
"kernel-worker" slug, two seconds before its parent failed with the same
error and pushed again. While the parent is still running, or has already
failed with that error, the child's failure now syncs silently. When the child
does alert, it carries the parent's display name.

commits.headline: fix(push-gateway): send one token per fresh APNs session before fanning out
commits.body:
A new token-authenticated APNs connection allows one stream until the first
request validates the token, and refuses the rest. With every stream
started at once, a localhost HTTP/2 server that does the same delivered 1 of
17 tokens and refused 16 with NGHTTP2_REFUSED_STREAM. Each host now sends
its first token alone and fans out the rest once it answers (or after a
quarter of the deadline), and those get only the remaining time, so every
send still ends within one per-token deadline of the batch

commits.headline: fix(mobile): let a hub task's own Claude Code session sync silently instead of alerting
commits.body:
The session scanner records the CLI session a kernel task runs in as an
observed session parented to that task. Its lifecycle and prompts reached the
phone a second time under a generic "Claude Code" name. Events from an
observed session whose parent is a hub task now sync silently; sessions not
tied to a hub task alert as before.

commits.headline: fix(autojack): mark blockers only by metadata, not Blocked: wording
commits.body:
The `/^blocked:/i` text fallback still ran when raiseQuestion passed an
explicit null blocker, so an ordinary "Blocked: X. Skip or fix?" question was
escalated instead of judged. presentResult always sends explicit blocker
metadata, so the wording check added nothing. Drop it: an explicit blocker
(or, for callers passing none, the pending question checkpoint) is the only
signal.

commits.headline: fix(api): bound the top-level attention plan copies in excerpt mode
commits.body:
The serializer repeats context.attention's plan, detail and questions at
the top level, in camelCase and snake_case. Excerpt mode clamped only the
copy inside context, so a 200K-character plan review still came back at
about 1 MB with ?excerpt=true. Give attentionDetail the 8 KiB text cap and
its Truncated/FullLength flags, clamp attentionPlan and attentionQuestions
like context, and copy each result to its snake_case twin.

commits.headline: fix(agents): gate the PR-size rule on repository finalization everywhere
commits.body:
Codex review (#2017): an owner-autonomous operate run that asks for a PR got
the section, but requiresRepositoryFinalization() finalizes only change
workloads or a finalization policy, so the orchestrator never opens a PR for
it. Apply that predicate on every path, not just the legacy one. The
owner-autonomous positive test now uses a change workload; it had encoded
the Definition of Done's promise that the orchestrator creates the PR, which
the disposition code does not keep.

commits.headline: fix(agents): stop babysit continuations when the finalizer child is cancelled
commits.body:
Cancelling the finalizer child directly (task-control's cancelAgentTask)
kills its session and marks the row cancelled without touching the parent
signal or the attempt id, and the nested executor reports a plain failure.
The continuation loop therefore re-spawned up to three more finalizers on
the same PR. Read the child row after every run and stop on `cancelled`
with the existing cancellation-shaped result, keeping the row cancelled
instead of overwriting it with `failed`. A `failed` row stil

commits.headline: fix(config): pin ha-mcp Python via UV_PYTHON instead of --python
commits.body:
The hub's orphan cleanup uses the first non-flag uvx arg as a process-kill
pattern, so `--python /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14` would turn that path into
the pattern. Keep args as ["ha-mcp@8.5.0"] and set UV_PYTHON in the server env
instead; update the example description and .env.example note to match.

commits.headline: fix(config): pin ha-mcp to Homebrew Python for macOS Local Network access
commits.body:
macOS Local Network privacy denies LAN connections from uv's unsigned managed
CPython, which `uvx ha-mcp` picks by default, so every Home Assistant MCP call
failed with "No route to host" while internet traffic still worked. Pin the
interpreter to /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.14 (already allowed) and note in the
example config and .env.example that Local Network access must be re-approved
after a `brew upgrade python@3.14`.

commits.headline: Add bookshelf Lennard-home indicator automation
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: fix(autojack): escalate blockers instead of judging them, naming the agent
commits.body:
A blocked present_result now marks its owner question with the blocker, and
the AutoJack question router routes any marked question (or a `Blocked:`
question, or a pending checkpoint carrying blocker metadata) to a new
`blocker` tier: never judged, never auto-answered in any mode, and always
escalated to Jack at medium urgency, so it can no longer go out as a silent
passive push. Ordinary questions keep the existing judge path.

commits.headline: fix(mobile): keep blocking questions apart from FYI questions in needs-input dedupe
commits.body:
The needs-input dedupe key had dropped payload.status, which was the only
thing that separated an FYI raise_question from a blocking question on the
same task. A blocking question raised within 30 s of an FYI one was dropped
as a duplicate: no push, no feed row. Key on whether the question blocks,
which all three needs-input publishers set the same way.

commits.headline: test(api): run the task excerpt test in the gating suite
commits.body:
test/v1-task-excerpt.test.js was in no curated CI suite, so the
package-scripts wiring guard failed and CI would never run it after this
PR. Add it to test:gating next to v1-agent-model-validation, which uses
the same disposable-database harness.

commits.headline: fix(agents): give the PR-size rule only to runs the executor finalizes
commits.body:
A legacy run with no execution spec, such as a qa-browser implement run,
reached the PR-size section even though requiresRepositoryFinalization()
says the executor never opens a PR for that profile. Use that predicate on
the legacy path. Also name the 900-line refusal as the slicing threshold,
since "exceed that" read as the 400-line target, which AGENTS.md keeps as a
checkpoint rather than a stop.

commits.headline: Soft barge-in 4/4: pause AJ on barge-in, resume after a backchannel (#1987)
commits.body: Wires the soft barge-in hold into the realtime voice agent. In barge-in mode a barge pauses AJ and shows HOLD; noise, empty/echo STT or a 1-2 word backchannel resume from the last natural pause, while 3+ content words, a stop word or sustained speech commit to the existing hard interrupt. Kill switch: VOICE_BARGE_SOFT_HOLD=false. Knobs documented in .env.example; adds the soft_barge conversation-smoke scenario.

commits.headline: fix(agents): run babysit finalizers until a terminal label
commits.body:
Claude-backed babysit finalizers were capped at 40 turns and any exit on a
non-terminal babysit:* label failed the parent outright, so PRs were left at
babysit:waiting-codex with nothing resuming them.

commits.headline: feat(api): bound task text behind an opt-in ?excerpt=true
commits.body:
GET /v1/tasks/:id for agent-fp-15eaf7f9 returned 1.7 MB: its ~165K-char
result and attention prompt recur in displayResult, lifecycle and context,
and the same row rides along on every /v1/tasks and /v1/tasks/running sync
the iOS app runs. With ?excerpt=true those three routes (and any task
response built by serializeAgentRunForResponse) cut result, displayResult
and attentionMessage to 8 KiB on a character boundary, cap every string in
lifecycle/context at 1 KiB and keep the last 5 toolsUsed en

commits.headline: style(push-gateway): drop whitespace-only line from the batch-send test
commits.body:
eslint --fix removed an unused disable directive after prettier ran and left a
whitespace-only line, which fails the prettier check in ci:preflight.

commits.headline: fix(mobile): persist hub questions from iOS conversations as one needs-input event
commits.body:
A kernel task dispatched from the iOS app carries the app's uppercase UUID
as its channel. The mobile event router passed it to the event store as the
conversation id, the store's schema accepts lowercase ids only, and the
failed write returned ok:false behind a void hook. No needs-input event for
such a task ever reached the feed.

commits.headline: Mute cues during a barge hold; settle it before an output-route switch
commits.body:
Cues play through their own player, so thinking and tool cues still
sounded over the user while AJ was held. playCue now skips everything
but error cues while a hold is open.

commits.headline: fix(push-gateway): send to device tokens concurrently inside the caller's window
commits.body:
The gateway sent to each registered token one at a time with a 30 s per-request
timeout, so the chat-server's 5 s abort fired first ("The user aborted a
request.") and no delivery receipt was recorded.

commits.headline: Add draft Lennard-home indicator for bedroom bookshelf strip
commits.body: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.headline: Soft barge-in 3/4: hold coordinator and TUI hold indicator (#1986)
commits.body: Adds the barge hold coordinator (src/voice/barge/hold-coordinator.js), which ties the soft-hold decider, controller barge capture and playback pause together, plus the TUI HOLD badge, Ink chip, barge.hold bridge event and runtime.status.bargeHold. Neutral until the wiring PR constructs the coordinator.

commits.headline: feat(agents): carry the PR-size rule in kernel coding prompts
commits.body:
AGENTS.md states the 400/900 changed-line rule ~55K chars in, past the
4000-char conventions cap in prompt-builder and Codex's 32 KiB project-doc
cap, so implementers only met the 900-line finalizer gate after finishing an
oversized change. Add a short fixed "PR Size" section to runs that deliver a
PR (kernel change finalization, plain implement with external writes, and
owner-autonomous runs that ask for a PR); investigate, read-only,
workspace-only, and babysit follow-on runs do not get it.

commits.headline: Match the recovery interrupt shape test to the hold-aware helper
commits.body:
The source-shape test pinned the literal jitterBuffer.interrupt?.() call
after the recovery timestamp. Both recovery sites now interrupt through
interruptPlaybackForPreemption(); the test keeps the same order check
(fresh delivery token, timestamp, then interrupt).

commits.headline: fix(push): clamp live-activity contentState so it fits APNs and the gateway
commits.body:
A 164K-char attention_message was copied untruncated into the Live Activity
contentState.summary and re-sent on every presence re-register, tripping the
gateway's 64 KB body limit (ECONNRESET). APNs caps a Live Activity payload at
4 KB anyway, so clamp summary and currentStep by serialized UTF-8 bytes
(code-point safe, ellipsis-terminated). Drop an oversized approve/deny pair
instead of truncating the submit token the app echoes back.

commits.headline: Keep a barge hold paused through final-audio recovery
commits.body:
When streaming TTS failed during a hold and recovery chose to interrupt
playback, the two recovery branches called jitterBuffer.interrupt()
directly. That ended the hold's pause, so the recovered audio played
over the captured barge. Both now go through
interruptPlaybackForPreemption(), which re-pauses while a hold is
active; the recovered audio plays only if the hold resumes.

feat(reflection-pipeline): run the pipeline end to end as a workflow processor (#2013)
commits.body: ## What

commits.headline: Speak a held system-say fallback only after a resumed hold
commits.body:
Callers without a turn signal, such as the runtime-error reply, still
spoke after waiting out a hold that committed, putting a stale message
over the user's new turn. Hold waiters now receive the outcome, and
speakWithSystemSay skips after any wait that did not end in a resume.

commits.headline: Take the reviewed orchestrator and processor
commits.body:
pipeline.js and the processor as #2013 stands after review: a dry run
reports dry-run, and a past day reads only what its nightly run (00:00
America/Los_Angeles) would have seen.

commits.headline: Let an accepted short reply outrank a later unusable final
commits.body:
When a hold had an accepted "Yes" and a later segment whose final was
rejected, empty or timed out, settle() resolved on the newest result, so
the coordinator discarded the capture instead of passing "Yes" through
after AJ finished. settle() now resumes with the latest accepted reply
that has words, and falls back to the old rules only without one.

commits.headline: Soft barge-in 2/4: hold decider and controller barge capture (#1985)
commits.body: Adds the pure soft-hold decider (src/voice/barge/soft-hold.js) and LocalVoiceController barge capture (beginBargeCapture / endBargeCapture). Neutral until the wiring PR: nothing begins a capture yet.

commits.headline: Keep earlier segment results when a queued resume reopens
commits.body:
Reopening with a fresh decider dropped the first segment's accepted
reply, so "Yes" followed by a VAD misfire resumed and discarded the
capture instead of passing "Yes" through. The decider now has reopen(),
which clears a resume resolution and keeps every segment's result, and
the coordinator uses it.

commits.headline: Hold system-say fallback until a barge hold resolves
commits.body:
`say` bypasses the paused jitter buffer, so when both TTS providers
failed during a soft barge-in hold the fallback spoke over the captured
barge. It now waits for the hold to resolve. A committed hold has
already aborted the turn by then, so both TTS fallbacks pass the turn's
signal and report speech_cancelled instead of speaking.

commits.headline: Reopen a queued resume when new speech starts
commits.body:
A resume decided on a short final runs one tick later, and the decider
is already resolved by then. A speech-start in that gap was ignored, and
the queued resume then discarded the whole capture, follow-up included
("Yes" then "actually deploy it"). A speech-start now drops the queued
resume and decides afresh with a new decider anchored at the hold's
start, so maxHoldMs still bounds the hold.

commits.headline: Match stop phrases across hyphens
commits.body:
ASR can write a multiword stop cue as one hyphenated token ("hold-on",
"never-mind"), which never matched " hold on " and resumed playback
after the user asked it to stop. Stop-phrase matching now treats hyphens
as spaces.

commits.headline: Recognise stretched fillers squeezed to a single letter
commits.body:
Squeezing stretched letters to two still left "ummm" as "umm" and
"uhhhh" as "uhh", neither a known backchannel, so a long filler counted
as content and committed at maxSpeechMs. Tokens are now also checked with
repeats squeezed to one letter ("um", "uh"), alongside the two-letter
form ("hmm") and the token as written.

commits.headline: Treat laughter and filler spellings as backchannel
commits.body:
ASR writes laughter and fillers as "ha-ha", "hahaha", "hmmm", "mm-mm" and
the like. Only the exact backchannel words were recognised, so a laughing
barge counted content words and committed at maxSpeechMs, breaking the
rule that all-laughter speech keeps holding. A token is now backchannel
when, with stretched letters squeezed, it is a known backchannel, a
laughter run (haha, hehe, heh), or only backchannel parts joined by
hyphens. Real words such as "he", "hi" and "well-known" still count.

commits.headline: Report dry runs as dry runs, and read a past day as its night ran
commits.body:
A run with publish: false wrote nothing but reported its outcome as
published; it now reports dry-run. A run given a past day read pull
requests, commits and heartbeats up to now, so a rerun could post about
later events as that night's story; it now reads only what existed by
that night's run, 00:00 America/Los_Angeles after the UTC day (D+1 07:00
UTC in daylight time, 08:00 in standard time), or now if that is sooner.

commits.headline: fix(voice): await nonempty SSE drafts before release
fix(babysit): drop over-reaching sentinel and skip failed PR-create calls
commits.body: Second local Codex pass flagged two gaps in the first fix:

commits.headline: Check for an unanswered segment directly, not by timestamp
commits.body:
settle() treated "oldest unanswered closedAt > 0" as "a segment is still
waiting", so with a zero-based replay clock a segment that closed at 0
looked answered and a newer misfire resumed past its pending final.

commits.headline: fix(babysit): detect production tool-event shapes and require terminal labels
commits.body:
Local Codex pre-PR review found three P1 gaps that let the very PRs this gate
targets bypass it:

commits.headline: Time out only the segment whose final never came
commits.body:
The final timeout resolved the whole hold as soon as the oldest segment
had waited finalTimeoutMs, even when a newer segment had only just closed
and its final, possibly real words, was still on the way. A timeout now
settles just that segment, and the hold resolves once no segment is open
or still waiting.

commits.headline: Track each barge segment's pending final separately
commits.body:
The decider kept one pending segment and one deferred final, so with
three segments in a hold a short final from segment 2 plus a misfire on
segment 3 resumed before segment 1's real final arrived, and that final
was then ignored. Every closed segment now waits for its own final in a
map; real words still commit from any segment, and the hold resumes only
when no segment is open and every closed one has answered short or empty.

commits.headline: feat(babysit): require babysit evidence for every PR an agent run opens
commits.body:
The orchestrator's babysit finalizer is the intended PR path, but a run can
open a PR directly (granted github.create_pull_request tool, gh pr create, or a
companion repo finalized outside the primary receipt). assertRequiredFinalization
Receipt only fires when requiresRepositoryFinalization is true, so a PR opened on
a lane where it returns false slipped through with no babysit — how AutoApp
PR #427 (branch agent/kernel-worker/59799793) landed without /babysit.

commits.headline: fix(voice): preserve concurrent successful draft release
Keep discarded STT turns until their final lands; remember partial content
commits.body:
The controller evicted discarded turn ids once more than 16 piled up, so
after enough quick backchannels a slow final for an early one passed the
check and reached the agent as a new turn. Ids are now kept until that
turn's final request ends, or two minutes pass, never evicted by count.

commits.headline: Report follow-up steps that fail after the post is live
commits.body:
publishDraft now returns the memory and Slack steps that failed after
the post went live (#2009). The pipeline result and the processor
summary carry them, and the processor warns: a run in processor mode
has no backfill for a missing publication memory, which would drop the
post from the next night's dedupe list unnoticed.

Take the reviewed publish stage

instead of rejecting.

commits.body: ## What

commits.headline: Hold the rest of an in-flight write when playback is paused
commits.body:
With no cap set, a multi-slice entry that backpressured after its first
write ignored a pause() issued while it waited: once the player drained,
the inner loop wrote the remaining slices even though isPaused() was
true. The loop now hands the unwritten rest back to the queue when
playback is paused as well as when a cap is active.

commits.headline: Take the reviewed research stage
commits.body:
research.js as #2007 stands after review: a link a results page repeats
is one result and one read, and two pages with the same passage still
give a card from each page.

commits.headline: Take the reviewed judge and review stage
commits.body:
review.js as #2006 stands after review: a failed judge call is a failed
gate that keeps the original, not a tie, and a reviewer answering
'None.' flags no claims.

commits.headline: fix(voice): separate reset admission from turn ownership
Recheck the write-ahead cap after an in-flight write drains
commits.body:
When the cap was enabled while an uncapped multi-second entry waited on
player backpressure, the inner write loop resumed after the drain and
sent the rest of that entry without consulting the new cap. The loop now
hands the unwritten rest back to the queue, undoing its playback
accounting, so the cap is checked again before each further slice.

commits.headline: docs(voice): clarify clipping threshold wording

commits.body: ## What

commits.headline: Treat a failed judge call as a failed comparison, not a tie
commits.body:
When a judge call failed, createJudge fell through to 'tie', and the tie
rule then kept a revision that answered flagged claims although no judge
had compared it. A failed call now returns 'failed' (the second order is
not asked once the first fails), and a failed gate keeps the original.

commits.headline: Keep a card from each page when two pages share a passage
commits.body:
Cards were deduplicated by quote alone. When two pages gave the same
passage, the cards validator accepted one from each as two pages, then
the second card was dropped and the angle failed with "cards from 1
page(s)". A card is now a duplicate only when both its page and its
quote match one already kept.

commits.headline: Take the reviewed story gate
commits.body:
reflect.js as #2005 stands after review: a looked-up pull request reads
its merge state from pull_request.merged_at, as the collector does.

commits.headline: fix(reflection-pipeline): skip the title call for a draft that failed its checks (#2004)
commits.body: ## What

commits.headline: Chart only whole numbers in one honest unit
commits.body:
A chart number no longer traces to part of another number: not 41 in
-41, 3 in Qwen3, 5 in 3/5 or 2 in 2nd. "percent" counts as %, any other
word after a number (1.5k, 64 kilobytes) is a unit of its own instead
of joining bare counts, and shares written as "3 out of 5", "1 in 4" or
"3/5" stay off the axis like "3 of 5".

commits.headline: Count Ollama models as local in the role-model check
commits.body:
The check in the previous commit named anthropic and mlx as the providers
with an adapter, so a registered Ollama model such as local-uncensored was
refused with "runs on ollama; the reflection pipeline runs Anthropic and
local models only". The local adapter serves Ollama models, and main
resolves them, so only the OpenAI references should be refused. A sweep of
every id, alias, preset, role, tier and local tier in the catalog throws
for exactly the thirteen OpenAI ones.

commits.headline: Count a link a results page repeats as one search result
commits.body:
A search response can list the same link more than once. Each copy got
its own R number and its own read, so four copies of one page could
spend the five-read budget before a second usable page was reached.
Results are now deduplicated by link across and within responses, and
numbered here.

commits.headline: Keep the publish stage's dry run, chart numbers and records honest
commits.body:
A dry run with a chart no longer uploads it to WordPress: it renders
locally and previews the local file. A thousands separator is part of
a chart number, so 1,204 charts as 1204 instead of letting 1 or 204
through. Once the post is live, a failed memory write or Slack note is
logged, recorded and returned in `failures` instead of rejecting.

commits.headline: feat(reflection-pipeline): per-role model and effort selection (#2001)
commits.body: ## What

commits.headline: Read a looked-up PR's merged state from pull_request
commits.body:
The story gate's GitHub lookup reads an issue, and an issue read of a pull
request keeps merged_at under pull_request, so a merged PR was added to the
digest as closed. The collector already reads both places.

commits.headline: Read a reviewer's "None." as no unsupported claims
commits.body:
The review asks for "none" when nothing is unsupported. A reviewer that
shipped with "None.", "- n/a" or a quoted "none" had it read as a claim,
which sent the shipped draft through a revision, let a tie keep that
revision, and rewrote the title with "None." as the flag.

commits.headline: Base the barge-in toggle guard on audio already written
commits.body:
getPlaybackLeadMs() includes audio still queued in the jitter buffer,
which the cap holds back once it is on. Using it for the toggle guard
could keep barges on the hard interrupt for the rest of a long reply,
long after the old unbounded tail had played. The jitter buffer now
exposes getWrittenLeadMs(), the part already handed to the player, and
the guard only waits that out.

commits.body: ## What

commits.headline: Keep a barge hold paused across speech-lane preemption
commits.body:
When an essential reply preempts a preemptible tool narration, the speech
lane interrupted the jitter buffer directly. interrupt() clears the pause,
so the new reply could start playing while HOLD was still up and the
capture was still deciding. The preemption now re-pauses the buffer while
a hold is active: the reply queues behind the hold, plays if it resumes,
and is aborted with the turn if it commits.

commits.headline: feat(reflection-pipeline): verbatim evidence passages (#1995)
commits.body: ## What

commits.headline: End a barge hold over tail playback on manual interrupt or sleep
commits.body:
A hold can start while only speculative-release or tail audio is playing,
with no hybrid turn. Manual interrupt and sleep then had nothing to abort
and called controller.interrupt() directly: the controller dropped its
capture, but the coordinator stayed active and the jitter buffer stayed
paused until the hold timed out, leaving HOLD on screen and the tail
queued to resume. Both commands now stop playback first while a hold is
active, which cancels the hold and cuts the tail.

commits.headline: fix(slack): keep reply framing out of model routing
Fail a soft-barge turn whose backchannel never played
commits.body:
When the stimulus did not play, interruptionPlaybackStartedAt stayed
unset, so the outcome lookup fell back to the last hold anywhere in the
turn, and because the interruption was never attempted the status check
skipped it entirely: an earlier accidental hold that resumed could pass
the scenario without the backchannel being injected. The resume decision
now lives in resolveSoftBargeResume, which needs a played stimulus with a
start time, and an expect-resume turn fails unless it resumed.

commits.headline: Ignore the request end of a final that already produced a transcript
commits.body:
Parakeet emits a final's transcript (or rejection) and then its request
end. The coordinator read every final request end as an empty decode, so
a short final deferred while a newer segment was open was overwritten by
"empty": when that newer segment misfired after AJ had finished, the hold
resumed and dropped a short reply that should have passed through. The
coordinator now remembers which segments already answered and skips
their request end.

commits.headline: feat(reflection-pipeline): draft checker and evidence cards (#1994)
commits.body: ## What

commits.headline: Match the barge wake word on whole tokens
commits.body:
The wake-word check searched the transcript with its spaces removed, so
"auto jacket" contained "autojack" and hard-interrupted the reply as a
wake word. The wake word now has to be spelled by consecutive whole
tokens: "auto jack", "AutoJack" and "auto-jack" still commit, while
"auto jacket" stays a two-word utterance that resumes.

commits.headline: feat(reflection-pipeline): collector, reader and link registry (#1989)
commits.body: ## What

commits.headline: Keep the hard interrupt until the pre-cap playback tail has played
commits.body:
The write-ahead cap bounds only writes made after it is set. Switching
from wake-word-only to barge-in mid-reply left up to ~2 s already written
at the old unbounded pace, which a pause cannot retract, so the first
barge after the toggle showed HOLD while AJ kept talking. Enabling the
cap now records how long that written tail has left, and barges keep the
hard interrupt until it has played.

commits.headline: Record failed reflection pipeline cloud calls in the usage ledger
commits.body:
A rejected Anthropic call (timeout, 5xx, abort) skipped the adapter's
only ledger write, so workflow.reflection_pipeline would log no failed
attempts and its error rate would read lower than it is. The failed
call is now recorded with ok: false and its error name, then rethrown
to the role loop, the way the workflow llm step does it. Follow-up from
#1997 review (#1998).

commits.headline: Keep an earlier pending final in charge when a newer segment misfires
commits.body:
A misfire resolved the hold as a resume unconditionally. When a real
segment had closed and its final was still on the way, a short noise
segment that misfired in between threw that final away, so "please check
the deploy" never interrupted.

commits.headline: fix(slack): preserve assistant history deduplication
Leave an unset role effort to the model's default
commits.body:
resolveRoleModels filled every unset effort with 'medium' and passed it
to the cloud adapter as an explicit choice. Model selection rejects an
explicit effort on a model without effort levels, so model: anthropic-fast
threw 'Unsupported effort medium for claude-haiku-4-5' before the first
call. An unset effort now stays null, and the adapter applies medium only
where the model takes an effort.

commits.headline: Tie the soft-barge smoke to its own hold and add a recovery turn
commits.body:
The resume check accepted the last hold outcome anywhere in the turn, so
an earlier accidental hold that resumed could pass the scenario even if
the injected backchannel never crossed the gate. It now reads the first
hold resolved at or after the stimulus started playing.

commits.headline: Pass barge segment ids to the decider and wait out the playback lead
commits.body:
The coordinator now hands each capture event's STT turn id to the soft
hold decider, so a late short final from an earlier segment cannot
resume a hold the newest segment still owns.

commits.headline: Ignore late short finals from an older barge segment
commits.body:
When the user speaks twice during a hold and the first segment's final
lands after the second segment closed, a short or rejected final from
that first segment resumed the whole hold. Finals now carry their VAD
segment: a final from an older segment can still commit on real words,
but it can no longer resume or clear the newer segment's pending final.

Codex review on #1987:
- The local `say` fallback plays outside the jitter buffer, so a soft hold

  children, and a barge takes the legacy hard interrupt while any plays.
- The soft_barge smoke only proved the backchannel never became a user
  turn, which a hard interrupt that dropped its transcript also satisfies.

commits.body:
Codex review on #1984:
- A drain whose finish timer was already counting down completed under a
  pause, closing the cycle and dropping the rewind ring. pause() now clears
  that timer, finishDrain() waits while paused, and resume() finishes the
  drain once nothing is queued.
- Enabling the cap after a multi-second entry was queued left that entry
  unsplit, so it was written in one go. processQueue now writes one
  write-sized slice of an oversized entry and requeues the rest while the
  cap i

commits.headline: Measure continuous barge speech per segment and commit any speech at max hold
commits.body:
Codex review on #1985: speechStartedAt kept the first segment's start, so a
second short segment could reach maxSpeechMs early; and a hold that hit
maxHoldMs with VAD speech still open but only backchannel partials resumed
over a user who was still vocalizing. The clock now restarts on every
speech start, and max hold commits whenever speech was confirmed.

commits.headline: docs(mcp-sse): correct why route-shaped memory_ids are refused
commits.body:
The comments and parity doc said ".." normalizes to a viewer at "/"
whose HTML would be read back as a memory. The viewer moved to /viewer,
and GET / is now a JSON 404, so ".." reads as an unknown id and "by-tag"
gets GET /memory/by-tag's 400. Neither returns data. The pre-check stays:
the id lands in the URL path, and any route added under /memory/ later
would be reachable the same way.

commits.body:
The memory_id pre-check only took the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 form, so the
bridge refused ids the API accepts and stdio forwards: braces, a urn:uuid:
prefix, no hyphens, and the int(s, 16) grammar uuid.UUID parses with (0x,
underscores, whitespace, Unicode digits). It now applies that rule.

and garbled it ("Each operating://tine operating system..."); nothing
checked quotes outside the blockquote. Any quoted span of 8+ words must
now appear word for word in a card, the angle's evidence or a recent
post title.

commits.body:
From the v5 accuracy audits:
- A memory lookup re-added a memory the digest had (as "undefine" when

commits.body:

commits.body:
Gemma's story gate ran past its 6,000-token limit on every resample twice

commits.body:

commits.body:
25 of the last 30 AutoJack posts used the same four labels (First
hypothesis, The breakthrough, Anti-pattern, Playbook), and 9 of the last
20 closed on a "same family as the X post" callback. The template asked
for both: the Problem Breakdown format was that skeleton, the voice
section called its headings "the format", and the examples used it.

commits.headline: Give each draft its own shape, opening and ending instead of a template
commits.body:
Jack: the posts all follow one structure and end on "the anti-pattern".
23 of the last 30 published posts use the template's First hypothesis /
Breakthrough / Anti-pattern / Playbook lead-ins, and the pipeline's own
drafts converged too: five of seven opened on the same number and ended
on "Next step".

commits.headline: Point repairs at each dash, and replace any that survive in code
commits.body:
Two of four drafts in the first four-draft run died on em dashes that two
repairs did not remove: the note gave only a count. It now quotes where
each dash is, and when dashes are the only problem left after the
repairs, code swaps the post's own dashes for commas (never inside a
quote) instead of dropping the draft.

commits.headline: Leave page furniture that repeats the title out of the passages
commits.body:
On an arXiv abstract page every candidate passage was chrome that matched
the story through its title ("View a PDF of the paper titled ...", the
bare title line), so Gemma had nothing quotable from that page and the
angle failed for want of a second source. Paragraphs that repeat the
page title, or open like arXiv chrome, are no longer passages.

commits.headline: Split passages into sentences without losing text
commits.body:
The sentence matcher read the full stop in 1.2 or v0.7.0 as a sentence
end, and a global match skipped what it could not match, so a numeric
sentence came back as "0rc1, measured over 3,212 turns" and a quote could
start mid-sentence. Sentences now break only after . ! or ? followed by
whitespace and a capital or digit, and no text is dropped.

commits.headline: Keep raw PDF bytes out of the evidence passages
commits.body:
Bright Data can return a PDF as raw bytes, and passage extraction took
binary paragraphs whose PDF tokens matched story terms ("/Filter" for a
tool-filter story). Gemma rightly refused to quote them, and the angle
failed for want of a second source. Paragraphs with replacement
characters, PDF object syntax or too few letters are no longer passages,
so such a page counts as unusable and research reads the next result.

commits.headline: Exempt quotes from the style rules and match them by their words
commits.body:
The pipeline checker counted em dashes and banned phrases inside the exact
quotes it fills in from evidence cards, so a source that uses an em dash
failed a check no repair could fix. Style rules now apply to the post's
own words. The trial scorer does the same for its em dash check, and
matches a quote to its page by words in order, so Sonnet swapping a
source's em dash for a period (to meet the no-dash rule) no longer reads
as an invented quote; the Phase A audit found exactly that case.

commits.headline: Show the evidence cards to repairs and revisions, allow a second repair
commits.body:
Phase B's first run dropped a draft that linked one outside source: the
repair prompt carried the checker's note but not the cards, so the writer
could not see which card would add a second source. Repair and revision
prompts now list the cards, every card list numbers its source page, the
writer is asked for two sources rather than two cards, and a draft gets
up to two repairs.

commits.headline: fix(accounting): allow separators in tax preparation memos
Think only where it fits, retry a failed search, record rejected submits
commits.body:
The second smoke run published its first post, but the reviewer spent
three 5,000-token calls thinking and never answered, so the post went out
unreviewed. Thinking is now on only for the reflector, queries and picks;
cards, review and judging run without it, and the score fields are named
so Gemma's alphabetical field order puts the reason before the scores.

commits.headline: fix(accounting): recognize ae tax preparation spelling
fix(accounting): exclude tax preparation from payment hints
Write with thinking off, and record each role call's outcome
commits.body:
The pipeline smoke run on 2026-10-03 failed in the writer: with thinking
on, Gemma 4 spent both 8,000-token writer calls thinking (about 90,000
characters of thought) and never wrote the body. Writing roles now run
with thinking off; reflect, research, review and judge keep it. Sonnet,
whose thinking cannot be turned off, writes at low effort.

commits.headline: Read the night's pull requests through a dated issue search
commits.body:
list_pull_requests on automem fails inside the GitHub MCP server's own
output validation when a PR's head repo is null (a deleted fork), and
the collector lost every automem PR with it. An issue search filtered by
update date returns the same PRs, with the merge time nested under
pull_request, so the gateway's as-of-the-run filter and its compact view
now read it there too.

commits.headline: Group the trial's blind page by night so same-story drafts sit side by side
commits.body:
The page showed each approach's middle run, which for an approach that
skips the thin night is a skip with nothing to rank. Grouped by night,
every draft written from the same evidence is shown together under
letters shuffled per night, and the run table gains a decision column.

commits.headline: Leave thinking budgets off by default after a live check
commits.body:
On Gemma 4 the oMLX budget does close the thought (about 500 characters
of reasoning against 1,600-1,900 uncapped), but the model then reasons
on in the visible answer, and one capped reply ran to max_tokens. Uncapped
replies answered cleanly in about 9 s. Roles still carry their budgets
for a run that turns them on.

commits.headline: Score outside quotes by the scraped page, and count outside projects as outside
commits.body:
The self-reference registry lists outside projects (the MCP spec, LoCoMo,
mem0) as well as Jack's own, and the scorer treated every registry URL as
ours: a verbatim quote from modelcontextprotocol.io failed the outside
quote check. Only Jack's sites and repos are ours now.

fix(desk): read pending CI verdicts after a terminal babysit relabel
commits.body:
A PR whose CI was pending when babysit moved it straight to ready/blocked
vanished from the three label searches, so `pr checks` never ran and the
pending entry was dropped without its ci_pass/ci_fail edge (the common
CI fail -> blocked path). The direct `gh pr view` re-read now covers
tracked pending-CI PRs as well as Codex ones: open PRs rejoin the poll
with only their tracked labels, so the verdict is read as an off-label
pending entry; merged or closed drop silently.

commits.body:
oMLX closes the thought once a request's thinking_budget is spent and the
model goes on to answer. The local stream now sends one when a caller
asks (only with thinking on; no voice caller does), and each pipeline
role sets its own, with room in max_tokens for thought plus answer. A
rung 1 run spent 214 s and 40K characters thinking before dropping its
tool call; a role cannot do that now.

commits.headline: fix(desk): stable per-episode ids for tracker verdict edges
commits.body:
Delivering verdict edges before the state write (d41e855def) opened a
window: an append that lands just before a failed state write or a crash
is replayed on restart. The edge id now derives from the pending or
waiting-codex episode's `since` instead of the poll time, so a replayed
edge carries the same id and dedupes in the ring; a new episode always
gets a new id.

commits.headline: Chart only numbers the reflection's cited items contain
commits.body:
The reflector now gives chartable numbers as label: value pairs, and the
publisher keeps a point only when its value appears as a whole number in
the angle's cited evidence, so a chart cannot show an invented figure.

commits.headline: Run the reflection pipeline as a workflow processor and as trial arms
commits.body:

starts, reading past failed picks; an angle that cannot find them hands
over to the next one. The pick judge sees both drafts' evidence. A reply
cut off at max tokens or by the degeneration guard is sampled again
instead of taken as an answer.

commits.body:

commits.headline: fix(desk): emit codex_done when babysit moves a PR to ready/blocked
commits.body:
The tracker only searches the three in-flight babysit labels, so a PR
that went waiting-codex -> ready/blocked vanished from every search and
its Codex state was dropped as if closed; the plan's codex_done edge
never fired on the normal completion path. A tracked Codex PR missing
from the searches is now checked with one `gh pr view`: open and off
waiting-codex emits codex_done, still labeled waiting-codex (cut from a
capped search) stays in flight, merged or closed drops silently.

(reflect, research, write, review, judge) around code that collects the
evidence, fills in links and quotes, checks drafts and publishes. Not wired
into a workflow or the trial yet.

committed the CI/Codex transition before appending, so a failed append
lost the verdict edge for good. Undelivered edges now queue in the
tracker state file (pendingEdges, capped at 20) and are retried first on
every good poll, surviving restarts and relabels; transitions still
commit, so finished work is never shown in flight.

commits.headline: fix(mcp): keep the periodic zombie sweep off servers that are starting
commits.body:
The periodic sweep treated a server as live only once it was in `servers`,
which a start joins after initialization. A lazy start's freshly spawned,
tagged child therefore looked like an orphan. On 2026-10-05 08:00:18 the
sweep SIGTERMed mcp-toggl one second into the Morning Routine's lazy load,

first file whose filename words appeared in the prompt. "agent-run-cleanup"
matched every agent prompt ("agent", "run"), so every scheduled agent
workflow got the cleanup workflow's one tool, which the agent allowlist then
removed. A workflow's own tools are what keep them eager, so in agent lanes
weather, Toggl, FreeScout, Todoist, WordPress, bright-data, render_chart and
the Slack notify tool were all sent with defer_l

commits.headline: fix(models): audit raw Codex model variable values for drift
commits.body:
A Codex model variable holding an ID the catalog does not register
(`CODEX_MODEL=gpt-…`) audits as unresolved, so the drift check never
looked at it, although the router passes it to `codex --model` as is.
Treat an unresolved value in a `*CODEX_MODEL` variable as its own target
and audit unregistered targets against the served list, so a dropped raw
ID now fails `--codex-drift`.

commits.headline: fix(workflows): narrate scheduled runs only when something presents it
commits.body:
Every successful scheduled run asked the anthropic-mid preset for a
narrative, because success alone qualified, and so did an eligible
memory decision. The scheduler's legacy summary-memory write is a no-op,
so for a workflow without a Slack notification or Evernote log the only
reader was the execution record's result summary, and deterministic
maintenance jobs paid for a metered model call on every run.

commits.headline: fix(claude): keep bare-name tool calls in history after they run
commits.body:
The 2026-10-03 Daily Reflection published four drunk.support posts in one
turn. Sonnet 5.5 called `create_content` instead of the offered
`wordpress_create_content`. Execution resolved the bare name through
mcpClient.findTool() and created the post, but the next request's
reconcileToolUseReferences only accepts names in the round's tools array,
so it dropped the executed tool_use and its result and trimmed the turn.
The model never saw that it had published, and published again.

commits.headline: fix(worktrees): refresh pooled Claude worktree dependencies from the seed
commits.body:
The desktop app pools worktrees under .claude/worktrees/ and leases them
to new sessions with whatever node_modules they last had, so a lane could
start on a tree built for an older lockfile. ci:preflight then refuses to
run. Claude worktrees never ran the Codex dependency bootstrap, and the
bootstrap trusted any complete tree anyway.

Codex CLI refreshes for this login. A preset, role or model variable
whose target is no longer offered, has a retirement date, or has a newer
listed model in the same tier is marked with the suggested replacement,
and the command exits 1. It also exits 1 when the list cannot be read.

commits.body:
The Claude Code Codex plugin parks one detached app-server broker per
workspace and only its SessionEnd hook for that exact cwd stops it, so a
killed session, a hand-deleted worktree or a review run outside Claude Code
leaks it for good. On 2026-10-05, 46 brokers (38 over a day old) had the
macOS pipe budget at 512 bytes and hung SessionStart hooks; terminating the
38 restored 64 KB pipes.

an argument that is neither a flag nor a flag's value now names the target.
