commits.headline: fix(tasks): fail open on unknown status in attention predicate (#409)
commits.body:
Task.requiresUserAttentionPredicate() used a positive allow-list of active
statuses (pending, running, needs_input, queued, awaiting_input, nil, ""),
so it failed *closed*: any status not on the list — including unknown,
mixed-case, or padded values — silently dropped rows that the

commits.headline: fix(voice): hold a registered run to the plan's metric and arms
commits.body:
- A plan whose primary.metric was anything but action correctness still
  verified, and primaryDecision reported the action-correctness result
  under it. A registered run now refuses a plan whose metric is not
  action_correct, the only one this sweep scores.
- The plan's arms were not enforced: only the treatment and control had
  to be among --arms, so a run could drop or add arms. A registered run
  now takes its arms from the plan, refuses --arms, and refuses a plan
  that does not register

commits.headline: fix(voice): align emitted calls with the loop's record by position
commits.body:
Matching routedCalls by name and arguments could still credit the wrong
occurrence of identical calls: after "call, unrouted, grant, same call
again", the first emission took the second's dispatch, so an ordered
grant-then-call case failed and a call-then-grant case could pass.

commits.headline: fix(voice): require a registered budget and paired cases for the guard
commits.body:
- A plan that omitted thinkMaxTokens silently took the CLI default, which
  could change later without changing the plan's hash. A registered run now
  refuses a plan that does not register a positive thinkMaxTokens, and uses
  that value with no fallback. The committed plan registers 1100.
- A guard over a group whose cases all went unpaired held, since the empty
  result object is truthy and 0 >= 0. The guard now holds only over at
  least one paired case.

commits.headline: fix(voice): match dispatched calls by name and arguments
commits.body:
routedNames was matched to emitted calls by name, so when an unrouted
dev_browser(click) came before a routed dev_browser(snapshot), the click
consumed the snapshot's entry and was credited. The runtime plane now
reports routedCalls ({ name, args } as the loop parsed them), and the case
scorer matches each emitted call to one by name and arguments.

commits.headline: fix(voice): drain output before exit, refuse an empty --url, drop ties
commits.body:
- The CLI exited with process.exit(), which drops stdout still queued for a
  slow or pipe-limited reader, including the summary.json path. It now sets
  process.exitCode and exits once stdout and stderr have drained.
- An explicit --url that is empty (an unset shell variable) or not an
  http(s) URL is refused, instead of silently falling back to the
  environment's or the default endpoint.
- A thrown run can leave a case with an even number of verdicts. A tied
  case is now dropped as unpaired

commits.headline: fix(voice): refuse a --prereg file that is not a plan
commits.body:
main branched on the parsed plan's truthiness, so a --prereg file holding
null, false, 0 or "" skipped verification and every fixed-setting check and
ran an ordinary sweep. It now branches on whether --prereg was given, so
any parsed value goes through verifyPreregistration and is refused when it
does not verify. main is exported for the test that covers this.

commits.headline: fix(voice): credit only dispatched calls and forbid forced-final calls
commits.body:
- handledNames includes unrouted calls, which the loop answers without
  running a tool. The runtime plane now also reports routedNames, handled
  minus unrouted, and the case scorer credits expected calls from it, so a
  grant-only tool called before its grant can no longer pass a case.
  handledNames keeps its meaning for the gauntlet predicates that read it.
- A forbidden tool emitted in the forced-final response (exhaustionCalls)
  now fails the case, like one emitted in a budgeted round.

commits.headline: fix(voice): require an odd count of usable seed bases
commits.body:
An even --seeds list let a case tie within an arm, and caseVerdicts counts
a tie as a fail, so a 1/2 control against a 2/2 treatment became a
discordant pair with no control majority. A seed base near
MAX_SAFE_INTEGER also left no room for promptSeed's per-case offset, so
distinct bases could collapse to one derived seed. usableSeedBases checks
both (via isUsableSeedBase), and the CLI refuses a list that fails it.

commits.headline: fix(voice): apply the plan's non-answer policy and keep one case's scoring
commits.body:
- summarize takes the plan's nonAnswer and tieRule. Under nonAnswer "drop"
  a non-answer run gives its case no verdict, like a harness error, instead
  of counting as a fail. The frozen plan registers "fail" and "fail", which
  were already the effective defaults, so the sweep's scoring is unchanged.
- Unordered expected calls now each need a distinct call (the case-scorer
  fix below this PR). office-lights-one-left-on accepts one service call
  naming several lights, so it sets expect.shareCa

commits.body:
An unordered case ran calls.find over every call for each expectation, so
one handled set_timer satisfied two expected set_timer calls. Unordered
expectations are now matched to distinct calls by augmenting paths, so a
broad expectation listed first never keeps the only call a narrower one
fits. Ordered expectations were already distinct (strictly later rounds).

commits.headline: fix(voice): gate each arm's warm-up and pair only real latencies
commits.body:
- runArmBlock checks the presence gate before an arm's warm-up requests, not
  only before each case, so the next arm never warms while a voice client
  that attached during the previous arm is live.
- A run with no output has a null first-output time. Paired latency
  differences skipped nothing and counted it as 0 ms; pairs are now kept
  only when both sides are finite, and per-arm max ignores nulls too.

commits.headline: fix(recovery): validate the retry workspace before the transaction opens
commits.body:
The operator retry path awaited retainRecoveryWorkspace() inside
prisma.$transaction. That call runs git and stats the worktree, so the
transaction held SQLite's write lock (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) across real I/O.
Since Prisma runs on better-sqlite3 (#1905), a synchronous same-process
write landing during that window blocks the event loop in the busy
handler, the transaction cannot finish, and the write fails after
SQLITE_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS.

commits.headline: fix(db): run Prisma on better-sqlite3 so each process has one SQLite library
commits.body:
Prisma used libsql while raw modules used better-sqlite3, so every hub
process loaded two SQLite libraries that cannot see each other's locks.
When a better-sqlite3 connection closed while nothing else held the file
(a full restart), it deleted -wal/-shm from under Prisma's live
connection; Prisma kept committing to the deleted log and its checkpoint
overwrote the shared file. hub-unified.db was corrupted this way on
Sep 26, 27 and 28.

commits.headline: fix(agents): reconcile hook-only sessions only after a complete discovery pass
commits.body:
discoverRecentClaudeTranscripts caps projects, files per project and recent
roots. A capped pass can omit a live session's transcript, so treating an
unlisted hook-only row under the root as gone could complete a live session
at a prompt and close its phone request. Discovery now reports `complete`,
and the poller passes the hook-only root only after a successful, uncapped
pass.

commits.headline: fix(inbox): keep richer fields only for a re-delivery of the same event
commits.body:
Task pushes carry no notification_id, so every event of a task lands on
the one feed row keyed by its task id. keepingRicherFields merged the
stored row into any incoming item on that row, so a later question with
no embedded attention inherited the earlier question's options, and the
Inbox card could show and submit them. It now merges only when the event
id matches, which is what a re-delivery (background, then tapped) is.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): per-field pre-load rail merge; backslash reopens a dismissed drawer
commits.body:
The per-Hub file has three fields, and each now carries its own pre-load
edited flag: showing or hiding the rail before the load keeps the
operator's visibility but still takes the file's panes and width, so the
write-back can no longer erase saved panes. A dismissed drawer (Esc) is
available but not on screen, so the first backslash brings it back
focused rather than hiding its retained state. Codex P2s on PR #105.

commits.headline: fix(tests): wait for the detail fixture to finish serving
commits.body:
IdlessOptionalEndpointEventsDeduplicateAcrossRefreshesWithoutServerCursors
asserted endpoint.Served.IsCompleted straight after the second fetch.
UnityWebRequest completes on the last Content-Length byte, which can land
before the fixture's thread-pool continuation disposes the client and
exits, so a busy full suite occasionally saw an unfinished task and
failed with a bare "Expected: True But was: False".

commits.headline: fix(workspace): pre-load rail edits keep panes and width apart
commits.body:
An explicit "rail width auto" before the per-Hub file loads was a no-op on
the initial 0, so the file's width won; and a width edit alone marked the
whole rail edited, which would have discarded the file's panes. Panes and
width now carry their own pre-load edited flags: the load takes only the
untouched parts from the file and writes back when anything was edited.

commits.headline: fix(kernel): terminal CAS follows the cancelled orphan retry
commits.body:
Codex on #1865, round 8: cancelling the orphan retry attempt moves the
task's final-attempt pointer to it, so the terminal failed write's CAS on
the original attempt could never match and the task stayed running. The
terminal write now expects whichever attempt the task's pointer was left on.

commits.headline: fix(kernel): fail the task when the retry cannot return it to pending
commits.body:
Codex on #1865, round 7: if updateTaskStatus('pending') returned false after
the replacement attempt was created, the worker still announced the retry
and returned, leaving the task running with a finalized attempt and a queued
one nothing would claim. The transition result is now checked; on failure
the orphan attempt is leased and cancelled (best effort) and the task fails
on the terminal path with RETRY_TRANSITION_NOT_PERSISTED, the original
failure preserved.

commits.headline: fix(kernel): post-execution failures are fatal, and a retry that cannot be created fails the task
commits.body:
Codex on #1865, round 6. A failure after the agent ran was excluded from the
infra backoff but still matched the transient patterns (ETIMEDOUT from the
completion write), so the agent could be re-run anyway; post-execution
failures are now fatal for retry purposes. When createAttempt() throws after
the context already names the retry, the task used to stay running with no
attempt for anything to claim; it now fails on the terminal path with
RETRY_ATTEMPT_NOT_CREATED and the original failure pres

commits.headline: fix(kernel): only an explicit launch failure is pre-execution, and no probe outlives the grace
commits.body:
Codex on #1865, round 5. A returned `{ success: false }` means the agent ran
and reported the failure, whatever its text contains — a coding agent quoting
a repository panic or CLIENT_CLOSED must not be re-run — so every returned
failure is post-execution except the executor's explicit bridge preflight
failure (AGENT_BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE). And a probe that starts exactly at the
grace deadline now gets at most 1 ms instead of its full timeout, while a
zero-deadline call keeps its single full probe.

place those presses were dropped. The menu now uses OVRInput's standard

commits.body:

the SDK only assigns that property in Awake, so the saved scene held a
null hand. On device, CanInteractWith threw a NullReferenceException
every frame once hands were tracked, so pan and zoom never started and
the far ray behind it in the same selection group got no candidates.

commits.body:

its transcript row then, so it arms the new-content pill once; only an
already-correlated re-emission stays silent. The uncorrelated turn-zero
group folds from its heading like every other group.

CI would never have exercised any of them again. Wire all three into
test:gating and drop the two from the unwired baseline.

commits.body:
A delayed memory.retrieval from a rotated-away conversation is rejected
by the V2 ingest, so it no longer adopts a turn id or arms the pill. The
V2 Tools rows derive their status mark from the shared row state, so a
timeout reads as a failure on the Tools tab as it does in the tree.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): adopt ids from completions, unwrap result envelopes, accept succeeded
commits.body:
A tool.complete that arrives without its start correlates the unanswered
turn like a start does. Registry summaries and their cards read the
result with a {success, data} envelope unwrapped, matching the presenter.
The row state treats "succeeded" as success like the Tools views.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): stamp thinking turns from the envelope and count only new recalls
commits.body:
A thinking event that opens a turn before its transcript keeps the
envelope time instead of the wall clock, and thinking rows clamp to the
user's words like tools and routes, so Apply stays deterministic and the
thought never renders above its prompt. A re-emitted memory operation
replaces its row and no longer arms the new-content pill.

commits.headline: fix(tasks): answer /respond as soon as the reply is durable
commits.body:

resumed turn (94 s on 2026-09-25) while the iOS client gives up at 30 s
and cloudflared cancels the request, so a successful approval read as an
error on the phone.

commits.headline: fix(workspace): treat recall steps as transcript arrivals and hash their card fields
commits.body:
A correlated memory.retrieval now follows like a tool or route arrival
and arms the new-content pill when the operator is scrolled up; follow
runs after the V2 ingest so the new recall row exists. The transcript
cache stamps every recall field the row and card print, so an enriched
re-emission of the same operation re-renders.

It shows the background bridge's connection state, offers a reconnect action, and renders a live pairing QR locally with expiry handling and phone linking instructions. Polling and pending requests stop when the page closes, and navigation preserves the current conversation.

prs.title: feat(whatsapp): expose background connection and pairing status
prs.body: The background WhatsApp bridge could be running while disconnected, leaving AutoHub unable to explain whether a session needed relinking or the client needed updating. Add Hub endpoints that proxy authenticated connection status and reconnect requests while keeping the bridge token on the server, excluding expired pairing codes, and disabling response caching. Older bridges retain a basic health fallback with update guidance.

prs.title: feat(bridge): expose background connection recovery and pairing
prs.body: A running background bridge could be disconnected while exposing no usable pairing state. Keep REST available while unpaired, add authenticated connection/reconnect endpoints with expiring QR data, and report readiness only after WhatsApp authentication. Reconnects preserve session/message databases and serialize attempts; revoked devices rebuild device-bound client internals, stalled keepalives recover, and post-pair authentication has a timeout.

fix(plaid): tax refunds book to income.tax_refund, not refunds received
prs.body:
## Problem
`plaidIsRefund` flags any detailed PFC ending in `_REFUND`, and Plaid's `INCOME_TAX_REFUND` matches. The categorizer's tier-4 refund shortcut (`txn.source === 'plaid' && txn.is_refund`) runs before the PFC mapping, so a tax refund lands in `income.refunds_received`, which nets against revenue on Schedule C line 1.

prs.title: fix(plaid): only real refunds take the refund shortcut
prs.body:
## Problem
`plaidIsRefund` returned true for any Plaid transaction with `transaction_type: 'special'`, whatever its sign. Plaid's deprecated `special` type also covers card autopays, transfers, ATM withdrawals and payouts, not just refunds. The categorizer's tier-4 refund shortcut runs before counterparty memory and the PFC mapping, so all of those landed in `income.refunds_received` at 0.9 confidence and reduced reported revenue in the P&L.

prs.body:
## Why
airflow.autojack.ai said **STALLED** on 2026-09-27 with doors open on both facades and SE wind gusting 30+ km/h. Two causes:
1. The verdict is buoyancy-only. A well-flushed flat has no ΔT, so the harder the wind flushes, the more "stalled" it reads.
2. The hallway trend was effectively dead. The ZHA SNZB-02P reports only on a 0.1 °C change (about 1 sample/h), and the fit needed ≥3 samples in 15 min: that held in 3 of 2,826 windows over 10 days.
